name: mv
description: Moves or renames files and directories.

flags.description: Ask before overwriting an existing destination.
Overwrite without prompting (the default when not interactive).
Create a backup of each overwritten file (with a ~ suffix by default).
Move only when the source is newer or the destination is missing.

examples.explanation: Renames draft.txt to final-report.txt in the same directory — renaming is a move within the same filesystem.
Moves photo.jpg into the Pictures folder in your home directory.
Moves all .log files into an archive directory, verbosely and with confirmation before overwrites.
Replaces config.conf but keeps a backup of the previous version as config.conf~ (shown via ls).

about: mv performs the same action for files and directories. Within one filesystem it is a fast rename() call; across filesystems it silently falls back to copy-then-delete, which takes longer and needs enough free space.
useCases: Atomically replace a config file after editing a .new copy.
mistakes: Expecting a prompt before overwriting — plain mv overwrites silently; use -i.
Moving a directory into its own subdirectory, which fails.
warnings: mv overwrites destination files without asking by default. Combined with a wildcard typo this can destroy files.
